Yiqing Song | 宋一清
ScienceOther

I am an observational astronomer at the Max-Planck-Institut für Radioastronomie in Bonn, Germany, where I work as a postdoc researcher in the Star Formation and Galaxy Evolution group led by Prof. Dr. Amélie Saintonge. Previously I was a postdoctoral fellow at the European Southern Observatory and Joint ALMA Observatory in Chile, where I supported ALMA operation as an Astronomer on Duty and VLBI-friend. I obtained my PhD in Astronomy in 2022 at the University of Virginia and the National Radio Astronomy Observatory, supervised by Prof. Aaron Evans.

My current role focuses on exploring the technical challenges and opportunities for the Atacama Large Aperture Submillimeter Telescope via hands-on experimentation with datasets from APEX, IRAM30m, GBT and ALMA of the Milky Way and nearby galaxies. My main scientific interests lie in the fascinating chaos of local merger-driven starbursts, and I utilize a wide range of facilities including VLA , ALMA and JWST to characterize their spatially-resolved properties and study the underlying physics of star formation, supermassive blackhole accretion and feedback associated with these extreme, dense, dusty environments.

In my free time I enjoy all formats of science fiction, and spending time in nature.
